intro: Library assistants serve the public, organize materials and keep records accurate, skills that many office careers use. The closest of the 25 careers below are general office clerk work and library technician work, both at a 90% match, and 22 of the 25 options pay more than the $36,910 library assistants earn.
why_it_works: A library shift means checking materials in and out, helping patrons find what they need and keeping collections in order. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.38 out of 5 for this job and coordination at 3. Office, clerical and postal jobs use the same organizing skills, and all of the top 10 matches pay more. The gaps are persuasion and negotiation.
tips: Library Technicians earn $44,580, which is 21% more, often after a short certificate.
Executive assistants earn $76,590, or 108% more, and value your organizing skills.
Postal Service Clerks earn $62,130, which is 68% more, and work with the public too.

faq.q: What jobs can former library assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are general office clerks (90%), Library Technicians (90%) and administrative assistants (88%), based on O*NET 31.0. Administrative assistants earn $47,540, which is 29% more than the $36,910 library assistant median, with similar daily tasks.

faq.q: Which careers for library assistants pay more?
faq.a: 22 of the 25 matches pay more. Executive assistants earn $76,590 (108% more), Postal Service Clerks $62,130 (68% more) and title examiners $58,650 (59% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Executive assistant roles often expect a certificate or associate degree.

faq.q: Do library assistants need more education to switch?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than library assistants already have, including 8 of the top 10. In the closest match, 41% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and new clerks are usually trained on the job.

faq.q: What skills should library assistants learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, persuasion, negotiation and operations analysis. Social perceptiveness already rates 2.88 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so office software and business skills are the main steps toward better pay.
